available.statement: For a formal group F over the valuation ring R of a characteristic-zero complete discretely valued field K with normalized v, logarithm is a homomorphism F(M)→K; for integer r>v(p)/(p-1), log is an isomorphism F(M^r)→(M^r,+), with inverse formal exponential.

needed: For the actual finite dyadic extension F/Q2, with e=v_F(2), logarithm identifies U_F^(e+1)=1+m_F^(e+1) with m_F^(e+1), and (U_F^(e+1))^4=U_F^(3e+1).
derivation: Take the formal multiplicative law G(X,Y)=X+Y+XY over O_F; X↦1+X identifies G(m^r) with U_F^r. F/Q2 is complete of characteristic0 and normalized v_F, so p=2 gives threshold e. Both e+1 and3e+1 exceed e. The source supplies mutually inverse logarithm/exponential at both depths. The logarithm sends fourth powers to multiplication by4. Since v_F(4)=2e, multiplication by4 maps m^(e+1) bijectively onto m^(3e+1). Conversely, for y in U^(3e+1), exp(log(y)/4) lies in U^(e+1) and has fourth power y by injectivity of log. Thus the displayed equality is exact, not just an inclusion.
premises: The same finite local field F=L_v and normalized e=v_F(2) used in the beta local proof.
No elliptic curve or good-reduction hypothesis is needed for this G_m application.
boundary: The beta^4-on-units assertion, conductor support, e<=D and Herbrand change of numbering are separate inputs. No assertion at the excluded threshold r=e or arbitrary residue characteristic is imported into this application.

needed: Transfer beta triviality above relative break3e over F=L_v to absolute upper groups over Q2 beyond max(4D²,3e), with no factor [Lprime:Q].
derivation: F/Q2 is Galois because L/Q is Galois. In a finite Galois tower M/F/K write G=Gal(M/K), H=Gal(M/F), Q=G/H. The lower definitions give H_t=H intersect G_t. The upper quotient theorem gives |Q^u|=|G^u|/|H intersect G^u|; differentiating psi_Q(phi_G(t)) gives |H_t|/|H_0|, the derivative of phi_H, and both vanish at0. Hence H intersect G^u=H^(psi_Q(u)); pass to finite quotients for the absolute group. Since psi_Q has derivative at least1 for u>=0, psi_Q(u)>=u. The already established normal-closure estimate bounds the last upper break of F/Q2 by4D²; thus G_Q2^u lies in G_F for u>4D². For u also>3e its subgroup index psi(u)>3e, so the previously established beta triviality applies. Since e<=D and U0=4(DG0)², max(4D²,3e)<=U0.
incoming: Relative beta upper break<=3e from local Artin norm compatibility and the separately supplied G_m logarithm.
boundary: Not a theorem for an arbitrary non-Galois F/K; beta and actual field are fixed first. Does not establish the cochain or relative beta bound.

needed: The actual two-dimensional r_ell has conductor exponent at most2+2U0<=E0, and at most2 at p>R.
derivation: For ell!=p, the Artin conductor equals codim(V^I)+Swan(V). The lower weighted-codimension formula becomes the upper-numbered integral of codim(V^(G^u)) over u>0. Actual wild action vanishes aboveU0 and each codimension is at most2, so Swan<=2U0 and tame codimension<=2. With U0=4(DG0)² and E0=10(DG0)² the asserted bound follows since(DG0)²>=1. For p>R>=D the local extension degree is belowp and hence tame. On G_F the good-reduction Tate module has trivial inertia; the actual beta has trivial wild part because beta² is tame and p is odd. Absolute wild inertia is contained in G_F, so it acts trivially on r_ell and the conductor is at most2. Infinite tame unipotent action, if present, does not enter the finite wild integral.
incoming: The already proved actual r_ell restriction and its finite wild image.
